startingPoint.finding: RC36 established exactly-one effect rows only when the receiver marker and modeled effect shared one SQLite transaction.
startingPoint.openBoundary: No separate sink database, external process effect, multiple physical hosts, or physical actuator had been tested.

primaryEvidence.role: Official outbox event router documentation identifies a unique event ID as a duplicate-removal key and separates aggregate ordering from event identity.
Official Kafka 4.1 design limits its native atomic processing boundary to Kafka topics and states that other destination systems must cooperate.
The OASIS specification defines ExactlyOnce as source retry plus destination duplicate filtering and distinguishes acceptance, acknowledgement, and application delivery.
Primary position paper motivates message-based state-machine patterns when global distributed transactions are unavailable or impractical.
Official implementation description bounds all-or-none crash behavior to changes within one SQLite transaction.

question: Can an atomic receiver inbox/outbox followed by an independently durable idempotent sink eliminate loss and duplication across every preregistered response-loss and process-crash cut, while preserving the boundary between a modeled sink row and a physical effect?
causalChain: A delivery ID and outcome digest enter the receiver.
The receiver commits its inbox and durable outbox in one local transaction.
A relay retries the same event ID until it observes a sink acknowledgement.
The sink commits its inbox marker and modeled effect row in one different local transaction.
Only after that acknowledgement does the receiver mark the outbox delivered.
Independent database and history reconstruction adjudicates cardinality, identity, and recovery.

competingProtocols.name: DUAL_WRITE
competingProtocols.claim: Committing the receiver inbox before a separate outbox write is recoverable without another durable intent.
competingProtocols.separatingPrediction: A crash after inbox commitment cannot leave an accepted delivery with no replayable outbox event.
competingProtocols.rejection: A reachable crash-stable receiver inbox with no outbox, or no healthy path from that state to sink completion.

competingProtocols.name: EARLY_OUTBOX_ACK
competingProtocols.claim: The relay may mark an outbox delivered before the sink commits because it still intends to send it.
competingProtocols.separatingPrediction: Every delivered outbox marker implies a matching sink inbox and exactly one sink effect across a crash.
competingProtocols.rejection: A delivered outbox can survive while the sink has no inbox or effect.

competingProtocols.name: NON_IDEMPOTENT_SINK
competingProtocols.claim: At-least-once relay retries are sufficient even when the sink effect and duplicate marker are not atomic.
competingProtocols.separatingPrediction: Lost acknowledgements and crashes never make the sink effect count exceed one.
competingProtocols.rejection: Any reachable execution with two or more sink effects for one event ID.

competingProtocols.name: ATOMIC_OUTBOX_IDEMPOTENT_SINK
competingProtocols.claim: Atomic receiver inbox/outbox plus retry and atomic sink inbox/effect preserve at-most-once safety and regain completion after a finite fault prefix.
competingProtocols.separatingPrediction: All reachable states satisfy M1-M5, and every accepted state has a healthy suffix to one delivered outbox and one sink effect.
competingProtocols.rejection: Any invariant violation or any accepted reachable state without a healthy completion path.

model.finiteState: Ten variables: receiver inbox, receiver outbox, delivered marker, sink inbox, sink effect count saturated at 2+, four volatile intents/acknowledgements, and whether a crash occurred.
model.enumeration: Breadth-first fixed-point enumeration from the empty state for all four protocols.

invariants.M1: No crash-stable receiver inbox orphan without an outbox.
invariants.M2: The sink effect count never exceeds one.
invariants.M3: A sink inbox exists if and only if exactly one sink effect exists.
invariants.M4: A delivered outbox implies a committed sink inbox and exactly one effect.
invariants.M5: Every sink commit has a receiver inbox and outbox origin.
invariants.M6: Every accepted reachable state has a fault-free path to the terminal one-effect state.

model.independence: A separate Python implementation must reproduce every state count, transition count, pass/fail verdict, and shortest counterexample trace.
model.stopRule: Do not proceed to the process experiment unless P4 is the unique qualifier and the independent audit matches every registered model check.

confirmation.topology: One physical Windows host; separate Python receiver process, Node relay process, Python sink process; one SQLite file per receiver and one different SQLite file per sink case.
confirmation.databaseMode: Rollback journal, synchronous FULL, foreign keys enabled.
faultCases: Receiver process exit before inbox/outbox commit.
Receiver process exit after inbox/outbox commit but before HTTP response.
Sink process exit before inbox/effect commit.
Sink process exit after inbox/effect commit but before HTTP response.
Relay exit after a successful sink response but before outbox acknowledgement.
Receiver exit after delivered-marker commit but before acknowledgement response.
Fifty concurrent deliveries of one event ID to the sink.
Conflicting digest, malformed event ID, and malformed digest controls.

criteria.C1: Receiver precommit failure retries as created and later replays.
criteria.C2: Receiver postcommit response loss retries as replay.
criteria.C3: Sink precommit failure leaves the outbox pending; retry creates one sink effect.
criteria.C4: Sink postcommit response loss leaves the outbox pending; retry is a sink replay with one effect.
criteria.C5: Relay failure after the sink response leaves the outbox pending; retry is a sink replay with one effect.
criteria.C6: Loss of the receiver's delivered acknowledgement leaves the committed outbox delivered and no pending event after restart.
criteria.C7: Fifty concurrent sink attempts yield exactly one created response, forty-nine replays, and no missing response.
criteria.C8: Conflicting and malformed inputs are rejected without another effect.
criteria.C9: Every case has one digest-consistent delivery→outbox→sink inbox→sink effect row chain and both SQLite files pass integrity_check.

confirmation.independentAdjudication: A separate Node program reads every SQLite file read-only, reconstructs case denominators and crash outcomes from history, and recomputes every synthetic HMAC receipt.
stopRules: Preserve any failed first run and seal an amendment before changing a protocol, invariant, denominator, fault location, queue capacity, or code.
Connection failures count as missing responses, never as replays.
Do not call a sink database row a physical action.
Do not infer multi-host or partition tolerance from loopback processes.
Do not widen a deterministic finite fault matrix into an unbounded liveness claim.

uncertaintyBudget.model: Boolean control state and a 0/1/2+ effect count omit timing, capacity, retention, and unbounded histories.
uncertaintyBudget.implementation: Receiver and sink share one Python codebase; the independent audit diversifies the checker but not the service implementation.
uncertaintyBudget.network: Loopback HTTP and request-level response loss do not reproduce packet reordering, asymmetric partition, routing, TLS, or DNS failure.
uncertaintyBudget.storage: Process exits exercise SQLite recovery but not disk loss, correlated power failure, filesystem corruption, or controller-cache behavior.
uncertaintyBudget.sampling: Seven deterministic cases and fifty concurrent duplicates are a fixed test matrix, not an operational failure distribution.
uncertaintyBudget.physical: Physical hosts = 1; physical or third-party side effects = 0.

safetyEthicsSecurity: Use synthetic digests, loopback endpoints, non-production keys, and modeled effect rows only. Do not connect the experiment to fabrication tools, payments, messaging accounts, personal data, or production credentials.
resultStateAtSeal: No model result, confirmation database, confirmation history, or audit result existed when this document was sealed.
nextRungIfQualified: Move receiver, relay or broker, and sink onto distinct physical hosts; inject asymmetric partitions and host loss; then replace the modeled sink effect with an independently instrumented hardware-in-the-loop counter whose idempotency record cannot share the actuator transaction.
